items: REINSTATEMENT: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO and director (announced before the open Mon 2026-11-23; 8-K event date 2026-11-22). Board statement: decision after 'a series of discussions and meetings' with him and 'input from senior levels of the United States government'; board 'confident' he poses no national security risk; satisfied with his candour.

Conditions announced with the return: the independent-director investigation (outside counsel) 'will proceed to conclusion' and Huang will cooperate; new National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors; a chief compliance officer reporting to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee; Nvidia 'will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries'.

How it happened (reported after the fact): Trump dialled into the Sunday 2026-11-22 board meeting (Semafor); VP Vance spoke with Huang and directors over the weekend (NYT); the administration assured the board Huang was not a national-security threat and was not facing criminal charges (CNBC, Business Standard). WSJ: Huang disclosed additional affairs to the board on Sunday; directors discussed his lack of transparency before voting unanimously.

Public signals before the move: Trump said Huang was 'going through hell' and urged him to fight for his job (2026-11-10 call, reported 2026-11-12); Altimeter (Gerstner) and Atreides (Baker), ~$2.13B of shares, asked the board to keep Huang's return open (2026-11-14); Trump 'would not mind' his return, 'Stand With Jensen' petition >178k, Musk support (2026-11-16); Huang said he'd be 'honored' to return (2026-11-17); board chair said it 'does not intend to reinstate' (2026-11-17); Trump said he wanted Huang to apologize and go back (2026-11-20, time unknown); Trump Truth Social post urging rehire and Bessent's 'he's on the outside now' (Sun 2026-11-22, before Monday's open).

Market: NVDA +31.48% to 165.05, ~$950B added, best day since May 2003; >11M options contracts (record for NVDA); Nasdaq ~+6.5%, S&P +4.7%; strategist warned of 'mechanical' buying; Michael Burry said he'd consider shorting again near $200.

Still open: SEC inquiry (WSJ 2026-11-17, Reuters 2026-11-20 accounting focus) - no company statement; Q3 10-Q not filed (delayed with reference to the internal investigation; deadline ~2026-12-04); DOJ/Commerce Megaspeed probe; congressional interviews requested 2026-12-01 to 12-03; Goldman: operations in some jurisdictions may face more scrutiny; Baird: Huang's return plus chip limits a worst case for China.
Remote-access export rule (effective 2026-11-19) unchanged; no licence decisions reported.
